During this battle, Daniel Sickles' Third Corps was overwhelmed by James Longstreet as it defended the Peach Orchard and the Wheat Field. On the first day of this battle, Harry Heth's division clashed with dismounted cavalry under John Buford before reinforcements under John Reynolds arrived. Edward Everett gave a two-hour speech at the site of this battle. On the second day of this battle, a bayonet charge by Joseph Chamberlain ended the successful defense of Little Round Top. The final day of this battle featured Pickett's Charge. Name this "high water mark of the Confederacy," a July 1863 Civil War battle fought in Pennsylvania.

One member of this political party gave his name to a group of boys who were conscripted to work in the coal mines during World War II; that minister was Ernest Bevin. This party eliminated capital punishment under Harold Wilson, but lost power after the Winter of Discontent. A prime minister from this party oversaw the creation of the National Health Service after taking over from Winston Churchill during World War II. Clement Attlee led this party, whose second-most-recent prime minister spearheaded its "new" version and backed Bush's invasion of Iraq. Name the British political party whose leaders have included Gordon Brown and Tony Blair.

He's not Napoleon, although this man sent in Marshal Soult to put down the Canut Revolt in Lyon. His head was depicted transforming into a pear in a political cartoon. The September Laws were passed after Giuseppe Fieschi killed 18 people around this man with a twenty-barreled monster weapon called the "infernal machine." Both Guizot and Adolphe Thiers led governments for this Duke of Orleans. This man came to power after the Three Glorious days, which ended the reign of Charles X. Name this "citizen king" of France who came to power in 1830 during the July Revolution.

The Roberts Commission was created to justify this policy, and the Ringle Report was withheld to avoid public outcry over it. John DeWitt carried out this policy after the issuing of Executive Order 9066. Photographers Dorothea Lange and Ansel Adams documented this event as it occurred in camps such as Manzanar. This policy's legality was upheld in the 1944 Supreme Court case Korematsu v. United States. Suspicion of a certain ethnic group led to, what forced relocation of descendants of the Asian foes of the United States following that nation's attack on Pearl Harbor?

Near the end of this war, John Talbot was defeated at the Battle of Castillon. Froissart reports that Jack Goodfellow, or Guillaume Cale, led the Jacquerie uprising during this war. Briefly suspended by the Peace of Bretigny, this war began at the Battle of Sluys. Charles d'Albret was killed during a battle in this war that was preceded by the St. Crispin's Day speech. A cavalry charge across a muddy field during this war was repulsed by one side's longbowmen at a battle won by Henry V. Name this long war fought between England and France that included the Battle of Agincourt.

One rebellion during this ruler's reign was partially put down by Peter Panin following the Battle of Kazan. This monarch issued the Nakaz and established the Hermitage museum. This monarch was called the "star of the north" and supported Stanislaw Poniatowski. Having gained power after the assassination of Peter III, this monarch made a deal with Maria Theresa and Frederick the Great to partition Poland. Advisors to this monarch included Gregory Orlov and Gregory Potemkin. This woman was a patron of both Diderot and Voltaire. Name this "enlightened" tsaritsa of Russia.

Nazi party member John Rabe had a significant role in safeguarding hundreds of thousands of civilians during this event. A safety zone established and governed by western businessmen and missionaries was created during this event, saving some two hundred thousand. One infamous incident during this event was the "kill one hundred people with a sword contest" that was "won" by Toshaki Mukai. It is still omitted in many Japanese textbooks. For 10 points name this atrocity of the Second Sino-Japanese War, during which three hundred thousand civilians were murdered and twenty thousand women raped in the namesake Chinese city.

In this state, US troops attempted to attack lava beds near Tule Lake in the Battle of the Stronghold, a victory for Native American chief Captain Jack in the Modoc War. Commodore Sloat became military governor of this state after claiming it for the United States; its other governors included William B. Ide and Stephen Kearny. John C. Fremont began a revolt that led to the creation of the Bear Flag Republic of this state. Thousands of people flocked to this state following the discovery of Gold in Sutter's Mill in 1849. Name this state which contains many missions established by Junipero Serra in locations like San Diego and San Francisco.

This man stated that "We will not walk to Canossa" following Pope Pius IX's rejection of his country's ambassador. A conference organized by this man protected the right to free trade in the Congo basin. The training and appointment of clergy were made state responsibilities when this man passed the Falk laws. He chatted with the captured Napoleon III after the Battle of Sedan, which ended a war he provoked by editing the Ems Dispatch. This man's "culture war" against the Catholic Church was known as Kulturkampf. This man engaged in realpolitik and is famous for his "blood and iron" oration. Name this "Iron Chancellor" of Prussia.

This king visited his sister while travelling as "Count Falkenstein." The treaty of Versailles was strengthened by this man's marriage to Isabella of Parma. One of this man's reforms was an attempt to quell a peasant revolt in Horea. This man extended religious freedom to Jews with his Edict of Tolerance, which was released a year after his Patent of Toleration. This man became co-regent after the death of his father Francis I. This brother of Marie Antoinette was succeeded by his younger brother Leopold I, who undid this man's liberation of the serfs. Name this enlightened son of Maria Theresa.

In this conflict, William Hicks' army was completely destroyed at the Battle of El Obeid, and following that battle, the victor enlisted the help of the Hadendoa tribe, known as "Fuzzy-Wuzzys." Garnet Wolseley was sent to relieve a key city during this conflict, but arrived two days after General "Chinese" Gordon's force had been defeated and slaughtered. Following the death of this conflict's instigator, an army under Horatio Kitchener crossed south from Egypt and won a decisive victory at the Battle of Omdurman. Name this colonial war in Sudan started by a Messianic leader.

Two people were tried for manslaughter following this event and were acquitted, although they later lost a civil suit and had to pay $75 per victim. These two men, Isaac Harris and Max Blanck, were initially found guilty of violating Section 80 of the Labor Code. Josephine Goldmark and Rose Schneiderman used this event as motivation to continue pressing for better working conditions, and it was investigated by future Labor secretary Frances Perkins. Beginning on the 8th floor, the victims of this event were unable to escape due to padlocked doors. Name this 1911 industrial disaster which struck a garment factory in the Asch building in Manhattan.

During this war, William Augustus lost to Maurice de Saxe at Fontenoy. The treaty that ended this war renewed Great Britain's rights to the asiento. This war began shortly before Frederick the Great's victory at Mollwitz as part of his invasion of Silesia. Known as King George's War in America, this war was precipitated by a decree that violated Salic law. That Pragmatic Sanction came into effect after the death of Charles VI. This war was ended by the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle. Name this war that ended with the retention of a certain throne by Maria Theresa.

The trial of Leo Frank in this state for the murder of Mary Phagan precipitated a 1915 revival of the KKK. The last major Confederate victory in the Western theatre was fought in this state, at a battle in which George Thomas distinguished himself as the "Rock of Chickamauga." Henry Wirz was executed for his role in the administration of a prison camp in this state where 12,000 Union prisoners died; that prison camp was Andersonville. William Tecumseh Sherman became famous for his "March to the Sea" across this state. Name this state where Sherman captured Savannah.

The first modern instance of these events occurred after a victory by Lothar von Trotha in German South-West Africa. Orhan Pamuk's acknowledgement of one of these violated his home country's Article 301. One of these events occurred between the Hutus and Tutsi. Parts of Europe make it a crime to deny that one of these actions occurred, while Turkey prohibits discussing the Armenian one. Name these deliberate and systematic actions intended to wipe out massive segments of a population, the most famous example of which was the Holocaust.

This ruler is featured prominently in the Itinerarium Peregrinorum et Gesta Regis Ricardi. This man managed to escape from the Battle of Montgisard by mounting a racing camel after being defeated by the "Leper King," Baldwin IV. This man's namesake "tithe" was collected in England and France after he captured the city Baldwin was King of, and he famously offered Guy de Lusignan ice water after capturing him near an extinct volcano at the Battle of Hattin. This man replaced his predecessor Nur ad-Din as ruler of Syria and founded the Ayyubid dynasty after capturing Egypt. Name this Muslim leader whose capture of Jerusalem prompted the Third Crusade.

One tradition holds that any prayer made between this man's pulpit and his grave will never be refused, and another tradition holds that an empty grave next to the tomb of this man is waiting for Jesus to fill it. An angel once gave this man a white donkey to ride to Jerusalem and had earlier appeared to him on Mount Hira, where he asked this man to "recite." Forces loyal to this husband of Khadijah were victorious at the Battle of the Trench and had previously accompanied him on the hijra. Name this man whose actions and words were recorded in the Hadith and who received the Quran from Allah, the foremost prophet of Islam.

One king with this name defeated Hermann of Dorpat, who was fulfilling a papal bull issued by Gregory IX. That victory by a king with this name was the subject of a Sergei Eisenstein film. A pope with this name issued the Inter Caetera and settled disputes between Portugal and Spain over the New World with the Treaty of Tordesillas. Savonarola claimed that that Borgia pope was corrupt. Another ruler with this name lent it to a city in Egypt with a lighthouse listed among the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Identify this name given to "the Great" son of Philip II of Macedon.

This man eliminated the post of princeps senatus, increased the number of quaestors and praetors, and doubled the size of the Senate from 300 to 600. After hearing of Cinna's death, he started a rebellion that ended with his victory at the Battle of the Colline Gate. As quaestor, he diplomatically convinced Jugurtha to surrender during the Jugurthine War. After consolidating power, he had thousands of enemies killed by routinely publishing lists of them in the Forum with the promise of reward money for their deaths during his namesake "proscriptions." name this dictator of the Roman Republic and rival of Marius.

This president signed the Budget and Accounting Act and made Charles Dawes director of the newly created Bureau of the Budget. This politician gave the speech nominating William Howard Taft at the 1912 Republican Convention and appointed Taft as chief justice of the Supreme Court. Party leaders decided to back this man in a "smoke-filled room" of the Blackstone Hotel. This man ran for president promising a "return to normalcy." His Secretary of the Interior, Albert Fall, accepted bribes from oil companies in exchange for drilling contracts. Name this Ohio Republican whose administration was tainted by the Teapot Dome Scandal.

This ruler's civil service reforms include dividing public servants into thirty-three grades called mansabs and appointing wazirs to oversee revenue collection by local governors. This ruler built the Jama Masjid around the tomb of Salim Chishti in a capital he named the "city of victory," Fatehpur Sikri. This ruler ingratiated himself to his Hindu subjects by marrying Rajput princesses and by abolishing the jizya tax on non-Muslims, though he fought against the Hindu king Hemu at the Second Battle of Panipat. Name this successor of Humayun, the third and arguably greatest emperor of the Mughals.

While this man was away, his soldiers began playing football with the heads of prisoners during the Siege of Crema. This man, while destroying the Commune of Rome, captured Arnold of Brescia at the behest of Adrian IV. After the submission of Milan, lawyers sided with this man at the Diet of Roncaglia. This man's feud with Alexander III resulted in the Treaty of Venice. That treaty was signed after his cousin Henry the Lion refused to help him at the Battle of Legnano against the Lombard League. This founder of the Hohenstaufen dynasty drowned in the Saleph River during the Third Crusade. Name this Holy Roman Emperor who was known for his red beard.

This man was the main author of the instructions given to John Jay that eventually became Jay's Treaty, and he married the daughter of General Philip Schuyler. For preventing Lord Cornwallis from crossing the Raritan River after the Battle of Trenton, this man was appointed aide-de-camp of George Washington. This man wrote the Report on Manufactures and 51 of the 85 Federalist Papers. In George Washington's cabinet, he was the main rival of Thomas Jefferson and served as Secretary of the Treasury. Name this founding father killed in a duel with Aaron Burr.

The openly gay David McReynolds first ran in this election. In the primaries of this election, one candidate claimed to have "the Big Mo." Operation Eagle Claw's failure hurt its eventual loser, whose attacks on his debate opponent were disarmed by the line "There you go again." Championing a gas tax, independent John Anderson ran in this election as a third-party candidate. The winning vice president had attacked his running mate's "voodoo economics" in its primaries. The Iran Hostage Crisis was a major issue in, what landslide election, in which Jimmy Carter lost to Ronald Reagan?

One uprising in this city was the last major action of Operation Tempest. Some of this city's inhabitants committed suicide after tear gas was thrown into the Mila 18 bunker. Jurgen Stroop liquidated one neighborhood in this city before the Grossaktion deported many of its Jews to Treblinka. While visiting the site of a 1944 anti-Nazi uprising, Willy Brandt knelt in the middle of this city's ghetto. Following the unification of West Germany, a communist military alliance was formed by a pact named for this city. Name this capital city of Poland.

One man with this title was accused of filling an entire pool with wine to swim in, and earlier that man defeated Vahan the Armenian's Byzantine army near the Yarmouk River. The first man with this title launched the Ridda Wars, and the fourth man with this title fought off the claim of a dangerous widow at the Battle of the Camel. These figures included Uthman, whose death triggered a conflict called the First Fitna and the rise of the last "Rightly-Guided" one. Name these Islamic leaders, the first of whom in Sunni tradition was Abu Bakr, the successors of Muhammad.

After this king's brother married the commoner Anne Horton, Parliament gave him veto power over royal marriages with the Royal Marriages Act. Issue 45 of the North Briton mocked a speech made by this man, leading to the imprisonment of John Wilkes. This recipient of the Olive Branch Petition ordered William Howe to put down a colonial rebellion. This man's son of the same name served as regent after this king's urine became blue from porphyria. Name this mad Hanoverian monarch who lost the American colonies.

In one work, this man claimed that Hatuey refused to convert to Christianity after learning that Spaniards went to Heaven. This man lobbied for a set of laws that were watered down after a revolt by Peruvian landowners. Those were the New Laws. The Valladolid debate pitted this Bishop of Chiapas against Juan Ginés de Sepúlveda. This man supported the enslavement of Africans, although he attacked the encomienda system in "A Short Account of the Destruction of the Indies." identify this Dominican friar, who argued against the enslavement of Indians in the Spanish New World.

This entity was called "the biggest festival of [its] century" in a series of theses on it published by the Situationists. Claude Lecomte and Jacques Thomas were killed by sympathizers with this body. This government was set up in opposition to the Government of National Defense. Women supporters of this entity known as pétroleuses burned down buildings by throwing gasoline on them. This body abolished workers' registration cards and night work for bakers. Its leaders toppled the Vendôme Column and were rebuffed in their efforts to exchange Archbishop George Darboy. Its nominal president, Louis Blanqui, was arrested on the orders of Adolphe Thiers, who later led the assault on it known as the "bloody week". Name this body which attempted to establish a socialist regime in the French capital in 1871.

After this battle, Eteonicus was sent with ten triremes to overthrow the remainder of the losing side's stronghold in the north. Aracus was the nominal commander of the winning forces of this battle after the previous leader, Callicratidas, had been killed at the Battle of Arginusae Islands a year prior. Among the losing commanders were Adeimantus and Philocles. The winning fleet was stationed at Lampascus. A plan to move the fleet up to Sertos suggested to the losing commanders by Alcibiades was rejected. Conon escaped from this battle with only ten of his fleet's 180 ships. After facing their opponents for four days, Lysander crossed the Hellespont to insure victory, leading to the fall of Byzantium and eventual siege of Athens. Name this 405 B.C. Naval victory for Sparta over Athens, the last battle of the Peloponnesian War.

This ruler had success against the Portuguese under his admiral Piri Reis, but failed to take the city of Diu. This ruler had his State Architect create the Sehzade Mosque. His forces won the Battles of Preveza and Djerba. He successfully besieged Esztergom as part of the Little War. This man had his admiral Turgut lay siege to Malta as part of an ongoing battle with a group he drove out of Rhodes, the Knights of St. John. He recognized John Zapolya as a vassal after the former Hungarian king, Louis II, drowned fleeing this man's forces in battle. This only son of Selim the Grim had a navy commanded by Barbarossa. He codified the legal system, so that his subjects called him "The Lawgiver". Name this ruler who won at Mohacs and laid siege to Vienna, bringing the Ottoman Empire to the height of its power.

One man killed in a shootout during this event was a former Denver crime boss known for a swindle in which he wrapped money around certain objects. Soapy Smith was killed during this event, and Sam Steele led law enforcement during it. Residents of Circle City were among the first to respond to this event, which was sparked by actions of the Carmacks and Skookum Jim. The town of Dyea rose to prominence during this event and was connected to Bennet Lake by the Chilkoot Pass. Participants in this event were required to bring one year's worth of provisions by decree of the Royal Mounted Police. This event resulted in the founding of Skagway and Dawson City. Name this event in the Yukon, which saw the influx of thousands of prospectors.

This ruler's mother was Swiatoslawa, the daughter of Mieszko I of Poland. He signed a treaty at Oxford probably written by Wulfstan of York. Holy Roman Emperor Conrad II gave him Schleswig and Pomerania. His forces were positioned on Beacon Hill in a battle this man won, at which Thorkell the Tall killed Ulfcytel. He divided England into Wessex, Mercia, East Anglia, and Northumberland, and received the last Danegeld. At Assandun, he defeated Edmund Ironside. He had earlier married Emma of Normandy, the widow of Aethelred the Unready. Name this son of Sweyn Forkbeard and father of Hardecanute, a great Danish king who ruled England.

This politician's rise to prominence was supported by the Suite 3505 Committee, which included F. Clifton White. This man founded his state's Air National Guard and desegregated it two years before the US Armed Forces. This man co-sponsored the Joint Chiefs of Staff Reorganization Act with William Nichols. In one political campaign, this man promised "a choice, not an echo" and blundered by using the phrase "extremism in defense of liberty is no vice." This man won a contentious primary over William Scranton and Nelson Rockefeller, after which he employed a "Southern Strategy" in an election where he was attacked in the Daisy ad. This author of The Conscience of a Conservative was a five-term senator from Arizona. Name this Republican politician who lost in a landslide to Lyndon Johnson in the 1964 presidential election.

Carl Erdmann's thesis is one explanation of the causes of this event. This campaign inspired a series of attacks against Jews in Speyer and Worms led by Count Emicho. Kerbogha of Mosul failed to relieve a siege in this conflict. One side in this war was massacred at Cibotus. At the Council of Piacenza, envoys of Alexius I asked for aid in what would become this action. Armies in it were led by Raymond of Toulouse, Bohemond, and Godfrey of Bouillon, while its less organized leaders included Walter the Penniless and Peter the Hermit. It was preached at the Council of Clermont in 1095 by Pope Urban II. Name this military action in which Christians went eastward and successfully conquered Jerusalem.

A British force under Alexander MacKenzie-Fraser held one city in this nation for several months before withdrawing in defeat. One military leader from this nation had a French chief of staff named Joseph Sève and won victories at Homs and Konya. This nation's fleet was destroyed at the Battle of Navarino, where they were helping the Ottomans. In that war, and a later one against the Ottomans ended by the Treaty of London, this nation's forces were led by Ibrahim Pasha. Later, forces from this country allied with the English under Lord Kitchener to defeat the Mahdists and gain territory to their south in the Battle of Omdurman. Name this nation ruled in the nineteenth century by Muhammad Ali, a North African country whose cities include Alexandria and Cairo.

Mikhail Miloradovich was shot and stabbed while trying to reason with the rebels in this event. In its aftermath, its target imposed nation-wide censorship and set up a network of spies called the Third Section to enforce it. Sergei Muravyov-Apostol led a branch of this revolt by the Chernigov regiment. It had its roots in the Union of Salvation, and Kondraty Ryleyev and Pavel Pestel were among those executed after it. Prince Trubetskoy was to be made interim dictator in this event, but fled upon its failure. It took place in St. Petersburg's Senate Square, where military regiments assembled to pledge allegiance to the new czar mutinied instead. Name this failed uprising which aimed to replace Nicholas I with his brother Constantine, named for the month in 1825 in which it took place.

This man is theorized to have been bullied by Billy Hughes and subordinates named Cunliffe and Sumner after his easy victory in the "Coupon Election". His political downfall coincided with that of opposition leader Andrew Chamberlain following the Carlton Club meeting. Mackenzie King flexed Canadian muscle at the expense of this man's government in the Chanak Crisis, after which he resigned and was succeeded by Andrew Bonar Law. The House of Lords rejected the "People's Budget" that this man wrote while Chancellor of the Exchequer under H.H. Asquith. He promised to "make Germany pay" during the Paris Peace Conference. Name this Welsh Prime Minister who joined Vittorio Orlando, Georges Clemenceau, and Woodrow Wilson in negotiations to draft the Treaty of Versailles.

John F. Kennedy claimed Philip Mazzei was the originator of this phrase. In John C. Calhoun's Oregon Bill speech, he asserts that this phrase is "though less dangerous, is not less erroneous" than a similar one he calls "the most false and dangerous of all political errors." In his last debate with Stephen Douglas, Abraham Lincoln quotes John Pettit of Indiana as saying that this phrase is a "self-evident lie," and in the Gettysburg Address, Lincoln says the Founders were "dedicated to the proposition" that this phrase was true. It was consciously echoed it in the Declaration of Sentiments at the Seneca Falls Convention, which added "and women" to it. In another document, it is followed by the statement of the "unalienable rights" of "life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness." name this phrase which is the first of the truths that the Declaration of Independence holds to be "self-evident."

One line of this family failed to gain power after a cousin, Vieri, could not take over after Salvestro was forced into exile. This family's patron saints were Cosmas and Damian. Another of Salvestro's cousins was Averardo de' Bicci, whose son Giovanni founded a family institution. Popes from this family included Clement VII and the man who reconvened the Council of Trent, Pius IV. This family was buried in the New Sacristy of its namesake chapel designed by Michelangelo, whose patron was another pope from this family, Leo X. Another member of this family was queen during the St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre as the wife of Henry II of France. One member of this family was killed in the Pazzi Conspiracy, and its rule was interrupted by Savonarola. Name this banking family who ruled medieval Florence and whose members included Catherine and Lorenzo the Magnificent.

This leader achieved victory over one group by forcing the surrender of Hongan-ji in Osaka. This man built the first hirayamajiro, or flatland-mountain castle, at Azuchi. He was fatally attacked by his own general, Akechi Mitsushide. In one early victory, a thunderstorm helped him defeat the much larger force of Imagawa Yoshimoto at Okehazama. The enemy and eventual subduer of the Ikko-ikki, this leader provided the bulk of the matchlock-equipped army that withstood a cavalry charge by Takeda Katsuyori's forces at Nagashino. He placed one family's Yoshiaki on the throne as his puppet before deposing him in 1573. Name this man who overthrew the Ashikaga shogunate and united half of Japan, paving the way for his ally, Tokugawa Ieyasu, to found his own shogunate.

Archibald Cary imprisoned this man for five months on the charge of creating a public disturbance, and he was nicknamed "Son of Thunder." This man convinced a jury to pay only one penny in damages to Reverend James Maury during his participation in the Parson's Cause. This man introduced a piece of legislation that became an "alarm bell to the disaffected" by giving a speech which claimed "Caesar had his Brutus, Charles I his Cromwell." This man was first biographied by William Wirt, and he protested the Stamp Acts by introducing certain Resolves. Another speech given by this member of the House of Burgesses asked "Is life so dear, or peace so sweet?" name this founding father from Virginia who declared "Give me liberty or give me death!"

Lord Fisher resigned over this campaign. Liman von Sanders succeeded in fending off three attempts by Aylmer Hunter-Weston to capture Krithia in this conflict. A last-ditch attempt in this campaign saw Henry de Beauvoir de Lisle and William Birdwood attack Scimitar Hill and Hill 60, respectively. Birdwood was a commander of troops that had a namesake cove during this campaign. Charles Monro replaced Ian Hamilton as head of one side's troops during it. Winston Churchill supported this effort as first lord of the Admiralty. Heavy losses in this campaign were sustained by ANZAC forces, who were held up by Turkish troops under Atatürk. Name this attempt by the British during World War I to occupy Constantinople after crossing the Dardanelles.

With the help of his bastard brother Baudouin, this ruler defeated rebels from Liège at Brustem. He bought Ferrette from Sigismund II, and placed his enemy under house arrest during negotiations at Péronne. This ruler's father founded the Order of the Golden Fleece to celebrate his marriage to this man's mother, Isabella of Portugal. He was betrayed by the Italian Count of Campo-Basso. He placed Charles, duke of Berry, as nominal head of a group he started with Jean, count of Dunois, Francis II of Brittany, and others. This man fell off his horse and died while losing a battle to Rene II of Lorraine. This man led the League of the Public Weal against Louis XI, and he died at the Battle of Nancy. Name this son of Philip the Good, a duke of Burgundy whose death led to its decline.

In one incident in this city's history, John Ury was convicted by Daniel Horsmanden of instigating a slave insurrection aimed at burning this city down in 1741. The Buttonwood Agreement began one economic institution in this city, which erupted into violence after Charles Devlin was promoted by mayor Fernando Wood, causing this city's 1857 Police Riot. Tensions between Protestants and Catholics led to its Orange Riots, while workers became enraged that three hundred dollars could buy someone's way out of the army in its 1863 Draft Riot. Robert Moses did urban planning for this city, in which the Triangle Shirtwaist Fire occurred. Boss Tweed was a member of its main political machine, Tammany Hall. Name this metropolis home to Wall Street.

Lucius Arruntius commanded a division of this battle's winning side. Several years after this battle, its victor rebuilt a temple to Apollo on its site, when he founded nearby Nicopolis. Prior to this battle, the losing side landed in Greece and fortified near Patrae, but allowed the enemy to cross the Adriatic. One side in this battle was surrounded at the entrance of the Ambracian Gulf. This battle was completely lost when the rear of the losing side which had all the treasury ships hoisted sail and sailed away, despite the best efforts of winning commander Marcus Agrippa. The two sides in this battle had won earlier victories at Pharsalus and Philippi, respectively. Followed the next year by an invasion of Egypt, name this naval victory of Octavian over Marc Antony and Cleopatra?

One side in this conflict prepared Operation Cordage in case its ally attacked another country, but diverted its forces to Operation Musketeer instead. This conflict's beginning followed a plan laid out by Maurice Challe after the parties involved determined that the Tripartite Declaration issued six years prior was irrelevant. The instigators of this event had signed the secret Protocol of Sèvres. Lester Pearson won the Nobel Peace Prize after convening the UN Emergency Force to negotiate a ceasefire to this conflict, which caused the fall of Anthony Eden's government. It began when Israel invaded its neighbor, giving Britain and France the pretext to intervene to protect their own interests. Name this event started by Gamal Abdel Nasser's nationalization of an Egyptian waterway.

This ruler established a Lyceum at Tsarskoye Selo. In the Treaty of Fredrikshamn, he declared himself Grand Duke of Finland, which he had conquered. With noblemen like Nikolay Novosiltsev, he formed the Private Committee. He set up failed military settlements to deal with army food issues with General Arakcheev. This ruler fell under the influence of the mystic Barbara von Krüdener and was advised by Mikhail Speransky. After his nation lost the Battle of Friedland, he met with Napoleon on a raft in the Niemen River to sign the Treaty of Tilsit. With his Prussian and Austrian counterparts, he set up the Holy Alliance. He came the throne after the assassination of his father, Paul. Name this Russian czar succeeded by his brother Nicholas I who ruled from 1801 to 1825.

Trott Lott's attempt to exempt one of these groups from the Leahy Provision is detailed in a chapter of Generation Kill, and that group was at center of conflict in Plan Colombia. Due to involvement with one of these groups, Julius Chan was ousted as Prime Minister of Papua New Guinea. In addition to that example of these groups named Sandline, another of these groups was founded by Eric Prince and was investigated after the death of Scott Helvenston. After killing seventeen civilians in Nisoor Square, that group changed their name to Xe Services, and some of their employees were notably ambushed in Fallujah. Name these companies that are often used to escort VIP's in war zones, and whose most famous example was known as Blackwater Worldwide.

One leader during this period was advised by the Three Pedagogues. Another figure during this period controversially picked the anniversary of the Battle of Allia as the day to take on a new title. During this period, one man stabbed himself after losing the Battle of Bedriacum, while one account claims another man was executed at the Gemonian stairs. One leader in this period had ascended to power after supporting Vindex's revolt. This period saw the assassinations of Vitellius and Galba and the suicide of Otho. This period ended with the accession of a member of the Flavian Dynasty, Vespasian, ending a series of bloody civil wars that occurred shortly after the death of Nero. Name this period in AD 69 when the Roman throne changed occupants very quickly.

This man was the target of the 1980 Petition of Fifty. His military was criticized for shooting pro-independence demonstrators in a cemetery during the Santa Cruz massacre. This leader attempted to eliminate Western influence through "indigenization" of his country's official philosophy of "Pancasila." He was officially granted power in the Supersemar Decree. This head of the Golkar Party took power shortly after the 30th of September Movement against the previous administration's "guided democracy," and once in charge, he ordered the liquidation of his country's Communist party, the PKI. His "New Order" government invaded East Timor and was opposed by Megawati Sukarnoputri, the daughter of this man's predecessor. Name this Indonesian president from 1967 to 1998 who succeeded Sukarno.

A heavy rainfall prior to this battle prevented one side from taking advantage of the other's drunken celebration of George Washington's birthday. Prior to this battle one commander wrote a letter to "all Americans in the World" in which he promised "victory or death." Two months before it, Ben Milam was killed while leading a successful assault on the same site. According to legend, Moses Rose was the only one not to cross a line in the sand prior to it. James Fannin unsuccessfully attempted to join the losing side of this battle, and his forces were soon after massacred at Goliad. The losing side was commanded by William Travis, who was killed along with Jim Bowie and Davy Crockett. Name this 1836 battle where Santa Ana's Mexicans captured a San Antonio mission.

During this man's ministry, the Bishop of Rochester, Francis Atterbury, was arrested for his role in a Jacobite plot. His ministry survived riots protesting the potential reprieve of Captain Porteous, who had ordered troops to fire on civilians. He was opposed by Viscount Bolingbroke and William Pulteney, who founded the Patriot Whigs to attack him. He lost support after the death of Queen Caroline. While serving as Chancellor of the Exchequer, this man introduced the "sinking fund" and he later became First Lord of the Treasury after the South Sea Bubble collapsed. The War of Jenkins' Ear occurred during his ministry, which spanned the reigns of George I and George II. Name this Whig politician traditionally regarded as the first Prime Minister of Great Britain.
Sir Robert Walpole, 1st Earl of Orford

During one conflict, this man was opposed by the Cuñari, whose city of Tumebamba he destroyed. This man converted to Christianity at the stake so as to be garroted rather than burned alive, as offered by Vincente de Valverde. This man's father died around the same time as Ninan Cuyuchi. One of his generals, Chalcuchima, had been lured and captured, while another, Quisquis, continued to fight. This man was killed in Cajamarca among rumors that Rumiñahui was coming to his aid. He offered to fill a large room with gold and silver for his ransom, but the Spaniards didn't release him. This monarch had ruled from Quito, while his brother, Huáscar, was in the capital of Cuzco. After defeating Huáscar in a war of succession, he was captured by forces under Francisco Pizarro. Name this last Incan emperor.

The Guffey Coal Act was found to violate this legal provision in Carter v. Carter Coal Company. This provision was weakened in a case which struck down a ban on guns near schools, U.S. V. Lopez. The use of this provision to enforce the 1964 Civil Rights Act was upheld in Heart of Atlanta Motel v. U.S., and it was ruled to extend to labor relations in the Jones & Laughlin Steel case, which upheld the Wagner Act. The most notable case involving it was argued by Daniel Webster, and in that case, John Marshall decided that it allowed the regulation of steamboat trade between New York and New Jersey. It was empowered in Gibbons v. Ogden and it is found in Article I, Section 8 of the Constitution. Name this clause which grants congress regulatory power.

Omurtag solidified this country's northwestern border. One of its rulers lined the skull of Byzantine emperor Nicephorus I with silver and used it as a drinking cup. The first state of this name was established by Asparuh, while the second was founded by brothers Ivan and Peter Asen. One of its leaders led an uprising against Crusaders that captured Baldwin I at Adrianople. Another lost badly at Preslav. This country, once ruled by Samuel and Kaloyan, converted to Christianity under Boris I, and reached its greatest extent under Simeon the Great. Most of its army was decimated and blinded by Byzantine emperor Basil II, who became known as the "slayer" of its people. Name this country on the Black Sea whose capitals have included Turnovo and Sofia.

One speech delivered to this group alluded to the cleansing of the Temple of Jerusalem and the cleaning of the Augean stables, ending with a command to "take away that shining bauble." It established the Hale Commission, whose proposals for legal reform were largely ignored, and set up the High Court of Justice. This body was expelled and replaced by one sometimes called the Nominated Assembly, and was briefly reconvened to restore members excluded from it, who then dissolved this body to hold elections for a Convention Parliament. It came into existence after opponents of the Grandees were removed from its predecessor in Pride's Purge. Name this English Parliament succeeded by Barebone's Parliament, named for its status as a remnant of the Long Parliament.

This politician was the intended beneficiary of the enticement of Indiana "floaters" by William Wade Dudley in the "Blocks of Five" scandal. The first commemorative stamp was issued by this president's Postmaster General, a department store mogul. During his presidency, American sailors were attacked by a Chilean mob, sparking the Baltimore crisis. Unlike his Vice President, this man supported an ultimately unsuccessful bill to protect African-American voting rights, drafted by Henry Cabot Lodge. This running mate of Levi P. Morton worked with the Billion Dollar Congress to pass the McKinley Tariff and Sherman Antitrust Act. Name this man who was president from 1889 to 1893, in between the two terms of Grover Cleveland.

In the 1950s in this country, the socialist Leo Collard set off a second "school war" by requiring that teachers possess degrees. The St. Michael's Agreement made a federal state out of this country, whose independence movement broke out after a performance of La Muette de Portici. Léon Degrelle founded a fascist movement in this country called Rexism. One of its rulers, who used the Force Publique to subjugate its colonial subjects, was accused by the Casement Report of cutting off the hands of natives who did not produce enough rubber. In 1950, one king of this country abdicated in favor of his son, Baudouin. Fighting here during World War I occurred at Ypres (EE-pruh) and Flanders. Name this country whose king Leopold II colonized the Congo Free State.

Members of this movement used pseudonyms like "No Cheese" and "Pug Nose." The Chairman of the Ballarat League for mining reform, John Bassoon Humffray, supported this movement. John Collins was a figurehead of this movement that inspired the Plug Plot Riots. Feargus O'Connor edited their newspaper, The Northern Star. The "Physical Force" faction of it included John Frost, who led the Newport Riots. Thomas Carlyle wrote a pamphlet in support of this movement, which formed after the passing of the Reform Act of 1832. William Lovett wrote a document calling for annual Parliaments and constituencies of equal size among the six demands in this movement's namesake document. Name this British movement that demanded universal male suffrage.

This people was broken up into the northern Siling and southern Asding branches. According to one story, this group began raiding by sea after their king was left lame by a fall from a horse and couldn't ride anymore. That leader's son married the daughter of Roman emperor Valentinian III, Eudocia. The last king of this people was defeated after deposing his cousin Hilderic. They migrated upon invitation from Count Boniface to fight Placidia Aetia. That last king was beaten at Tricamarum and Ad Decimum and was named Gelimer. Many Alans joined them when they crossed the Strait of Gilbratar into North Africa, where they set up a kingdom for a century before being destroyed by Belisarius. Name this Germanic people which, under their greatest leader, Gaiseric, sacked Rome in 455 with a wanton destruction worthy of their name.

Arguments are made that this act is unconstitutional based on a Minnesota court case involving Jerome Daly. Several people who helped draft this bill were brought before the Pujo Committee earlier that year, and A. Piatt Andrew was among those who discussed it at a conference on Jekyll Island. This act, which was drafted by Robert Latham Owen, was a follow-up to one partly sponsored by Edward Vreeland that was passed in response to the Panic of 1907. This act was amended to create an "open market committee" by the Glass-Steagall act, and it was recommended by Nelson Aldrich and the National Monetary Commission. Name this 1913 act which set up a namesake central banking and money-issuing system.

This nation's inhabitants were once massacred under armistice by the Republican consul Servius Sulpicius Galba. Its king Denis founded the Order of Christ. Forces of this nation under Friedrich von Schönberg won the Battle of Montes Claros. This nation signed the Treaty of Windsor with England, who then helped this country defeat a larger force at the Battle of Aljubarrota. One leader of this country, whose death in battle inspired a messianic faith, was named Sebastian. The Aviz dynasty once ruled this country. Afonso de Albuquerque captured Goa for this nation, whose king John II signed the Treaty of Tordesillas with a larger nation. Name this nation which sent out explorers like Pedro Cabral and Vasco da Gama and who split the New World with neighboring Spain.

This man's first major battle was the Siege of Orchha in 1635, after which his father gave him a sword from which he took his regnal name. He convinced his youngest brother, Murad Baksh, to stake claim to the throne, and ostensibly supported him against the forces of his eldest brother, whom he defeated at the Battle of Deorai. This king's aforementioned brother was Dara Shikoh, and he created a code of Islamic law called the Fatawa-e-Alamgiri. He reinstated the jizya tax on non-Muslims abolished by Akbar. He killed Tegh Bahadur when the latter refused to convert to Islam, drawing the antagonism of that man's son, Gobind Singh, the last Sikh guru. Name this son of Shah Jahan, a Mughal emperor who brought the empire to its greatest extent.

This politician sued the Cumberland Telephone Company in his role as state Railroad Commissioner. Paul Cyr attempted to remove this politician from one position, and he personally campaigned for the reelection of Hattie Carraway. This man sometimes had an alliance with T. Semmes Walmsley and the Old Regulars political machine, and the Bloody Monday brawl broke out when oil interests attempted to impeach him as governor. His book My First Days in the White House laid the plans for a 1936 presidential run, and he was inspired by William Jennings Bryan to promise "every man a king." This advocate of the Share Our Wealth program was assassinated by Carl Weiss. Name this 1930s political boss of Louisiana known as "Kingfish."

The original Tower of Galata was destroyed during this campaign, which was organized by Thibaut III of Champagne at a tournament at Ecry. This campaign was chronicled by Geoffrey of Villehardouin, and a monumental bronze four-horse chariot was captured during it. Boniface of Montferrat was a leader of this campaign, which captured Zara despite the condemnation of Pope Innocent III. Enrico Dandolo brought the expensive help of Venice to this crusade, which established the Latin Empire. This crusade abandoned its original goal after being invited to depose the son of Isaac II Angelus by the man they would place on the throne, Alexius IV. Name this military campaign originally intended to retake the Holy Land that wound up sacking Constantinople.

This king was victorious at a battle preceded by a parhelion. He married his sister Margaret to Charles the Bold of Burgundy after angering his closest advisor by marrying a commoner. That advisor, his cousin, attempted to install this king's brother, George, Duke of Clarence, on the throne and was killed fighting against this king at the Battle of Barnet. This husband of Elizbaeth Woodville won an early victory at Mortimer's Cross and came back to the throne after a brief fall from power by winning at Tewksbury. His sons Edward and Richard were probably murdered in the Tower of London after his death. This king first came to power with the help of Richard Neville, who helped him overthrow Margaret of Anjou and her husband Henry VI. Name this leading Yorkist king during the Wars of the Roses.

Twenty years before this event, its instigators started a failed rebellion under Wang Lun. It was followed ten years after its end by the Eight Trigrams Rebellion. This uprising and a contemporaneous revolt of the Miao people forced an increase in the size of the Green Standard. One of its causes was the corruption of court favorite Heshen, who in fact embezzled money intended to put it down. It was subdued only after the Jiaqing emperor overthrew the Qianlong emperor. This event started as a protest against taxes by a society promoting Maitreya Buddhism, and aimed to replace the Manchus with the restored Ming dynasty, which had fallen some 150 years earlier. Centered in Hubei and Shaanxi, name this revolt against the Qing dynasty agitated by a group named for a flower

This woman championed educational reforms implemented by the Dutchman Gerhard van Swieten. She oversaw the implementation of the much-derided Chastity Commission and the Robot Patent. One of her children signed the Declaration of Pillnitz with his Prussian counterpart. Another granted limited freedom of worship for non-Catholics with the Edict of Toleration. That son, with whom she ruled for fifteen years, started the War of Bavarian Succession. This woman came to the throne after her father, Charles VI, signed the Pragmatic Sanction, and her accession sparked the War of Austrian Succession. Name this wife of Francis I and mother of Joseph II and Leopold II, an enlightened despot who effectively ruled the Holy Roman Empire for much of the 17th century.

This house's distinctive large nose supposedly signified its males' distinctive large sexual appetite. At the Congress of Vienna, this house was given Lucca and the promise of regaining Parma after the death of its queen. Its last king issued the September Laws after surviving an assassination attempt by Giuseppe Fieschi. They were supported by the Legitimists, and it is divided into the Montpensier and Marche-Vendome branches. One of its queens led the Day of the Dupes. Philip V of Spain established this family's ruling house in Spain, where it rules to this day. The first king from this dynasty issued the Edict of Nantes after defeating the duke of Guise and the last Valois king. Name this dynasty whose first French king was Henry IV and which ruled during the French Revolution.

Patrick Fermor, William Moss, and partisans from this country kidnapped Nazi general Heinrich Kreipe. Resistance forces during World War II in this nation included EDES and EAM-ELAS. Earlier, this country was ruled by the fascist Fourth of August Regime. After the war, communists set up a Provisional Democratic Government that was deposed in 1949. Lyndon Johnson once told off this nation's ambassador by saying "Fuck your parliament and your constitution" and calling this country a flea that could get whacked by the trunk of America's elephant. A military coup here led to the Regime of the Colonels and forced the son of former King Paul, Constantine II, into exile. Name this Balkan nation led at times by Ioannis Metaxas and Georgios Papandreou from Athens.

General Drouot, known as "the Monk", defended Gallows Hill during this battle. Josef Poniatowski died during this battle, which was preceded by the largest cavalry battle in European history, the Battle of Liebertwolkwitz. 20,000 troops were trapped trying to retreat from it after a bridge over the Elster River was destroyed. Early in this battle, Napoleon fended off attacks from Prince Schwarzenberg, but his army was defeated after the arrival of Leonty Bennigsen and Jean Bernadotte, the commanders of the Russian and Swedish sections of the Allied Army-Group. The varied participants on the winning side of this battle gave it its nickname, and it marked the end of French rule east of the Rhine. Name this 1813 battle often called the Battle of the Nations.

As commander of the Fifth Military District, this man ordered the removal of Texas Governor James Throckmorton for being an "impediment to the reconstruction." This man led an army to Texas in an attempt to persuade Emperor Maximilian to leave Mexico. This man was called east after his assault on Missionary Ridge near Chattanooga, and he won the Battle of Yellow Tavern, where J.E.B. Stuart was killed. While leading campaigns against the Plains Indians, he became associated with the maxim "the only good Indian is a dead Indian." At the Third Battle of Winchester he defeated Jubal Early, while leading a scorched earth campaign aimed at crippling Confederate infrastructure in Virginia. Name this Union cavalry commander who burned the Shenandoah Valley.

This action was deemed null and void in the Moscow Declaration. Earlier, it had been forbidden by Article 88 of the Treaty of St. Germain. One leader tried to manipulate a referendum to be held about this action by setting the voting age at 24. It led to the fall of the Fatherland Front. In the lead-up to this event, the murderers of Engelbert Dollfuss were granted amnesty. Kurt von Schuschnigg was replaced by Arthur Seyss-Inquart the day before this event, which gathered 99.7% approval in a plebiscite a month after it happened. Ostmark was created by this action, which was followed by encroachment into the Sudetenland. It was the first move in an expansionist policy based on the need for Lebensraum, or "living space". Name this annexation of Austria by Nazi Germany.

Naval forces prepared for one battle in this conflict by massing near Tangier Island. Sackett's Harbor was of strategic importance in this war, which saw the heroics of Laura Secord. Another battle in this conflict occurred after a failed rendezvous with Isaac Chauncey, and saw Gordon Drummond and Phineas Riall win a costly victory. Unrest leading to this war was partly caused by the Orders in Council, and before it, one side gained allies due to a raid on Prophetstown. The Battle of Bladensburg allowed one belligerent to enter the capital of the other. Name this conflict which saw battles at Lundy's Lane and Lake Erie, as well as the burning of Washington, a war between the United States and the United Kingdom named for the year in which it began.

This man created a squadron to provide transport for the royal family called the King's Flight. This figure tried to have Etienne Dupuch suppress the story of the murder of Canadian millionaire Harry Oakes. His first official act was to reverse the practice, initiated by his grandfather, of setting the clocks at Sandringham half an hour fast. His mistresses included Freda Ward and Thelma Furness. He became Governor of the Bahamas after marrying the former Mrs. Warfield, a move which gave him the newly created title of Duke of Windsor. This son of George V was replaced on the throne after just 11 months by his brother Albert, who took the name George VI. Name this member of the House of Windsor who abdicated from the English throne to marry Wallis Simpson.

This state's namesake platform argued that the Federal government cannot prohibit slavery in the territories and was written in response to the Wilmot Proviso. This state was home to the Fort Mims massacre, which occurred after troops under Major Beasley defeated Peter McQueen at the Battle of Burnt Corn in this state. This state's aforementioned platform was written by congressman William Yancey. Hamilton Fish and Charles Francis Adams negotiated with Great Britain to resolve claims arising from a ship named for this state. Jefferson Davis was inaugurated in this state's capital. During one battle in this state, David Farragut shouted "Damn the torepedos!" name this state which saw the Battle of Mobile Bay and a series of bus boycotts in Montgomery.

This ruler is seen holding a scepter with a fleur-de-lys in Abraham Cresques's Catalan Atlas. He commissioned Abu Ishaq as-Sahili to build mosques in a neighboring capital captured by his general, Sagmandia. This successor to Abubakari II kept his empire's capital at Niani but expanded it to cities like Djenné. Ibn Battuta travelled south from his homeland to visit this ruler's kingdom. He spent so profligately that, twelve years after his visit to Cairo, the gold market had still not fully recovered. That visit took place during a trip this man took with a caravan of 60,000 men to Mecca. Name this emperor of Mali who brought attention to himself with an extravagant hajj.

The Gablenz mission failed to prevent this war. General Flies' detachment was wiped out during one battle in this war, which saw the first combat mission of the Red Cross. During another battle in this war, General Fransecky led an advance through the Swiep Forest. In one theater of this war, Garibaldi's Hunters of the Alps won the Battle of Bezzecca. This war began after each side accused the other of violating the Gastein Convention. Italy allied with the winners and received Venetia for the effort. This war was ended by the Treaty of Prague, in which Schleswig-Holstein was given to the victors, who then established the North German Confederation, a predecessor to the German Empire. Name this war between Austria and Prussia that included the Battle of Koniggratz.

This ruler propped up the independence of Morgannwg and Gwynllwg as buffer states between his kingdom and that of Rhys ap Tewdwr. He gave border regions to relatively autonomous Marcher Lords. Earlier, with Henry I of France, he had put down a rebellion at Val-es-Dunes. He was advised by Lanfranc of Pavia in a campaign blessed by Pope Alexander II. This ruler died after the Siege of Mantes, where he fell off a horse. His advisor, William of St. Calais, compiled a census. He defeated the victor at Stamford Bridge in a clash depicted in the Bayeux Tapestry, in which that loser, Harold Godwinson, was killed. Name this duke of Normandy who ordered the compilation of the Doomsday Book and whose victory at Hastings paved the way for him to take over England.

This figure is given a supposed magical root by a man named Sandy. He remembers an incident in which Demby refuses to leave a stream and is shot by Mr. Gore. As a child he befriends Daniel and tricks older boys into giving him reading lessons by pretending to know more than them. He is changed when he reads a copy of the The Columbian Orator. He recalls speaking to the ships that sail by before relating his fight with the sadistic Edward Covey. He becomes a caulker at a Baltimore shipyard, but is forced to turn all his wages over to Hugh Auld. He marries Anna Murray and goes to New Bedford, Massachusetts, after escaping from Maryland. Name this character, a prominent abolitionist who relates the narrative of his life of slavery in a notable autobiography.

As Chancellor of the Exchequer, this politician set up the Post Office Savings Bank. This man wrote the massive but generally misguided essay collection Studies on Homer and the Homeric Age. A series of military reforms was put in place by his secretary of state, Edward Cardwell, and he settled the Alabama claims with the US. He won reelection with the Midlothian Campaign after returning to politics with a pamphlet attacking the sitting Prime Minister's indifference toward the Bulgarian Horrors. He introduced two bills on Irish Home Rule, which were rejected in his third and fourth sittings as prime minister. Name this Liberal Prime Minister of England, the long-time rival of Benjamin Disraeli.

One secret revolutionary society in this nation made the Cry of PugadlawinThree priests from this country known collectively as Gomburza were executed, leading to the Propaganda Movement, one of whose members founded La Liga. Its first president assembled the Malolos Congress. Andres Bonifacio founded this nation's revolutionary society Katipunan. This country was the subject of the 1946 Tydings-McDuffie Act, and its most populous city is named for an interwar president, Manuel Quezon. Battles fought here during World War II include Corregidor and Bataan. Name this Pacific island nation whose revolutionary leaders included Emilio Aguinaldo and Jose Rizal.

One formative event in this polity saw Walter M. Gibson removed by the Committee of Safety, and it was once dominated by the "Big Five" including Alexander & Baldwin. This polity saw John L. Stevens indicted and vindicated respectively by the Blount Report and the Morgan Report. Two rebellions led by a former Italian artillery officer, Robert William Wilcox, were defeated by republican forces here. The Newlands Resolution achieved a goal here opposed by Grover Cleveland, and in this territory Lorrin Thurston used the Bayonet Constitution to end the power of David Kalakaua. Name this territory where Sanford Dole served as president after the overthrow of Queen Lili'uokalani, and which was annexed by the United States as the fiftieth state.

This dynasty's first ruler abdicated after his second son, Shimin, seized the northern entrance to his palace and killed his brothers. One member of this dynasty, Ruizong, returned to the throne with the help of his son Longji and his sister Taiping, who was later forced to commit suicide. Longji, later known as Xuanzong, had as a consort Yang Guifei, who adopted a Turkic general who would later rebel against this dynasty. It was briefly interrupted by the rule of Empress Wu Zetian, who founded her own Zhou Dynasty, and it was greatly weakened by the An Lushan rebellion. Du Fu and Li Po were active during this dynasty. Name this dynasty preceded by the Sui, the cultural high point of Chinese civilization.

This figure called one institution "a vile pustule living on the blood and sweat of the peasants" in his pamphlet Monarchy and Democracy. This man was opposed by the National United Front for National Salvation. Choeung Ek stands as a memorial to a genocide this man ordered. Only seven people survived the prison camp he established codenamed S-21. He called himself "Brother Number One". He started his Super Great Leap Forward with a series of purges after proclaiming Year Zero and forcing the population of his country into farming collectives often called "killing fields". Earlier, he had overthrown Lon Nol's regime and changed the name of his country to Kampuchea. Name this onetime schoolteacher who led the Khmer Rouge as dictator of Cambodia.

These people historically selected four rulers from their Seven Council Fires, and one of their leaders was treated on his deathbed by Doctor Valentine McGillycuddy. 303 of these people were sentenced to be hanged following an uprising put down by John Pope. Forces from Fort Phil Kearny used Springfield rifles to fight off an overwhelming force of these people in the Wagon Box Fight. After the Battle of Rosebud Creek, George Crook withdrew from fighting these people, who initiated the Fetterman Massacre during a war which they fought in Powder River country. They signed the Treaty of Fort Laramie to end Red Cloud's War. These people destroyed the US 7th Cavalry Regiment in 1876. Name these people who won at Little Bighorn over George Custer and were the victims at Wounded Knee, a tepee-dwelling nation led by men like Crazy Horse and Sitting Bull.

This man was acquitted of fornicating with a Vestal Virgin and was later smitten with Aurelia Orestilla. He was derided for setting up a shrine in his house to revere a silver eagle. This man killed his brother-in-law Marius Gratidianus at the tomb of Lutatius Catulus on behalf of the latter's son. This man was killed after getting caught between Antonius and Marcus Petreius near Pistoria. Gaius Manlius led an encampment in Etruria that joined this man. Some of his allies were executed after envoys handed over signed documents detailing their plans. Sallust's first work was about this man's war. He was asked "How long must you abuse our patience?" in a speech whose orator lamented, "O tempora! O mores!" name this Roman who was brought down in 62 BC after four orations from Cicero berated and summarized his conspiracy.

The papal encyclical Dilectissima Nobis condemned this government. The CEDA was a faction during its tenure. Niceto Alcalá Zamora was succeeded by Manuel Azaña y Diaz as its president. This entity was plagued by a miners' strike at La Felguera, a result of the October Revolution during the rule of Alejandro Lerroux. It formed after the Pact of San Sebastian and was led at one point by the Popular Front. This government was defended by the Abraham Lincoln Brigade and other forces organized by COMINTERN and opposed by the Nationalists and Emilio Mola's fifth column. They executed Primo de Rivera, the leader of the Falange. Name this government that began with the 1931 abdication of King Alfonso XIII and ended when Francisco Franco won the Spanish Civil War.

A 1921 law in this nation allowed disputed territory to be colonized by Mennonites, who founded the city of Filadelfia. This nation lost a naval battle at Riachuelo, but a year later, won despite heavy losses at Curupayty. In another war, forces from this nation routed an army in the Campo Vía pocket led by German World War I veteran Hans von Kundt. One general from this nation, José Estigarribia, successfully besieged Fortín Boquerón and, later, Ballivián. Earlier, its army was decimated by the Campaign of Lomas Valentinas. This nation defeated Bolivia in the Chaco War but lost to forces led first by Bartolomé Mitre and later by the Duke of Caxias. In that war, this nation's opponents were Argentina, Brazil, and Uruguay. Name this nation which dictator Francisco Solano López drove to disastrous defeat in the War of the Triple Alliance.

This man successfully besieged Tailleburg and built strongholds like Château-Gaillard. London's Jewish population was massacred after several Jews brought gifts to this king's coronation. One legend holds that the minstrel Blondel attempted to rescue this man after Duke Leopold of Austria imprisoned him. This husband of Berengaria of Navarre had William Longchamp made chancellor. This monarch died while besieging the town of Chalus over a hoard of gold found by a peasant, and he had earlier won at Arsouf to capture Jaffa. This son of Henry II and Eleanor of Aquitaine took Acre, but failed to capture Jerusalem, and later concluded a truce with Saladin. Name this brother and predecessor of King John, a lion-hearted king of England who waged the Third Crusade with Philip Augustus and Frederick Barbarossa.

After this figure's position of "no war, no peace" wasn't accepted in the debate over a treaty, he resigned in favor of Georgy Chicherin. He denounced Zinovyev and Kamenev's opposition to the October Revolution in The Lessons of October 1917, but later joined with them. This man ordered the suppression of the Kronstadt Rebellion and was the head of the Red Army during the Revolution. He rejected a rival's theory of "socialism in one country" in favor of international "permanent revolution", and was soon removed from the Politburo and Central Committee. He was fatally attacked by Ramón Mercader with an ice pick in Mexico City, where he ended up after being exiled due to a split with Stalin. Name this Marxist revolutionary and founder of the Fourth International who led a failed struggle against Stalin's rise in the 1920s.

As president this man supported the Curtis-Crisp bill, which would have created a board to lend money to farmers during times of surplus, though earlier he vetoed a bill that would have allowed the government to buy crop surpluses, the McNary-Haugen bill. In the election he won, he defeated the man who accused Philetus Sawyer of bribery, and the opposing ticket featured Charles Wayland Bryan. Charles Dawes was the running mate of this man, who won an election over Robert La Follette and Charles W. Davis. As Governor of Massachusetts, this man put down the Boston Police Strike, and his Secretary of State signed the Kellogg-Briand Pact. Name this thirtieth president, who succeeded Harding and was notably "silent."

As an alternative to the swampy environs of this place, Henricus, was founded by Thomas Dale. Thomas West, Lord De La Warr, saved this location from disaster when George Percy's abysmal negotiating skills caused the "Starving Time." The House of Burgesses was established at this location in 1619. One leader of this city, tobacco entrepreneur John Rolfe, married the daughter of Powhatan, Pocahontas. John Smith was one leader of what first permanent British settlement in the modern United States, established in 1607 in Virginia?

This royal was almost killed by a grenade thrown by a Korean dissident during the Sakuradamon Incident. He advised his nation to begin "enduring the unendurable" after surrendering on behalf of his nation in the Jewel Voice radio broadcast. This regent led a country during the Mukden Incident, which served as a pretext for his nation's invasion of Manchuria. A picture of this man, also known as Showa, shows him next to Douglas MacArthur after renouncing his divinity. Name this emperor of Japan during World War II.

This event, at one point referred to as Operation Z, is the subject of a conspiracy theory centering on the McCollum memo. One participant in this event sent the Fourteen Part Message as a response to the Hull Note sent by the other participant. This event, which started with the signal "Climb Mount Nitaka," targeted Wheeler Field and destroyed the Oklahoma and the California. This event, which occurred on "a date which will live in infamy," also saw the destruction of the USS Arizona. Name this Japanese attack on a U.S. Naval base in Hawaii.

This country's worst school shooting occurred at Dunblane. One invasion of this country, a few decades after it became a part of a larger country, began at Prestonpans and climaxed at Culloden. This country's War of Independence saw it face off against Edward II. One leader of this country resigned as Guardian after the battle of Falkirk. Before ruling England, the House of Stuart ruled this country. Name this country whose leaders include Robert the Bruce, Mary, and William Wallace, which joined with England in the 1707 Act of Union.

One ruler of this empire feuded with his brother Dara Shikoh and imprisoned his own father. The Peacock Throne was the seat of the leader of this empire, whose first ruler defeated Ibrahim Lodi in battle. This empire was ruled by a man who abolished the jizya tax and a man who built the Red Fort and a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz at Agra. This empire's first ruler, Babur, was victorious at Panipat. Its emperors include Aurangzeb, Shah Jahan, and Akbar the Great. Name this Muslim empire that ruled India from the mid-1500s to the mid-1700s.

During a series of riots in this city, the Blues and Greens were two opposing groups. One building in this city is supported by "elephant's feet" and is named for its interior color. Enrico Dandolo redirected the Fourth Crusade to attack this city, the location where Belisarius slaughtered a mob in the Hippodrome during the Nika Riots. Mehmet II captured this city for the Ottoman Turks in 1453. Name this capital of the Byzantine Empire, which was renamed Istanbul by the Ottomans.

This man responded to the threat of multiparty elections in Hungary by ordering the deposition of Imre Nagy. One story about this man involves his response to Lorenzo Sumulong's indictment of his country's foreign policy. He denounced his predecessor in the "Secret Speech," which precipitated a "thaw" named for him. Under this man, the Partial Test Ban Treaty was signed in the wake of his unsuccessful attempt to put nuclear missiles in Cuba. Name this Soviet politician who de-Stalinized the Communist Party as Premier in the 1950s and '60s.
